chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ismail ibn Mansur, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Humran, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"Whoever marries while the moon is in the Scorpion (constellation), he will not see the good."

key_terms.الْحُسْنَى: The good, the best outcome, or the positive result/blessing of the marriage.
key_terms.الْعَقْرَبِ: The Scorpion (constellation), referring to a specific lunar mansion or astrological sign used in timing events.
key_terms.تَزَوَّجَ: He married, referring to the act of contracting marriage.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying when the moon is in the Scorpion constellation?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on Istikhara for marriage, this hadith highlights the Shia scholarly tradition of combining spiritual supplication with astrological timing (Tajribat al-Aqrab). It serves as a practical guideline for believers to avoid marital discord by steering clear of the 'Scorpio' lunar mansion, reflecting the integration of celestial signs with divine decree in domestic affairs.
